questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A liquid of density $600$ kg/m$^3$ flowing steadily in a tube of varying cross-section. The cross-section at a point $A$ is $1.0$ cm$^2$ and that at $B$ is $20$ mm$^2$. Both the points $A$ and $B$ are in same horizontal plane, the speed of the liquid at $A$ is $10$ cm/s. The difference in pressures at $A$ and $B$ points is ________ Pa.
questions.solution:
Using the equation of continuity:

$A_A v_A = A_B v_B$

$(1.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times 0.1 = (20 \times 10^{-6}) \times v_B$

$v_B = \dfrac{10^{-5}}{2 \times 10^{-5}} = 0.5$ m/s

Using Bernoulli's equation for a horizontal tube:

$P_A + \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_A^2 = P_B + \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_B^2$

$P_A - P_B = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho (v_B^2 - v_A^2)$

Substituting the given values:

$P_A - P_B = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 600 \times (0.5^2 - 0.1^2)$

$P_A - P_B = 300 \times (0.25 - 0.01)$

$P_A - P_B = 300 \times 0.24 = 72$ Pa

Answer: $72$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spherical liquid drop of radius $R$ acquires the terminal velocity $v_1$ when falls through a gas of viscosity $\eta$. Now the drop is broken into $64$ identical droplets and each droplet acquires terminal velocity $v_2$ falling through the same gas. The ratio of terminal velocities $v_1/v_2$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity of a spherical drop of radius $r$ falling through a viscous medium is given by Stokes' law:

$v = \dfrac{2}{9} \dfrac{r^2 (\rho - \sigma) g}{\eta}$

From this relation, the terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of the radius of the drop:

$v \propto r^2$

When the large drop of radius $R$ is broken into $64$ identical droplets of radius $r$, the total volume remains conserved:

$\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = 64 \times \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$

$R^3 = 64 r^3$

$R = 4r$

The ratio of the terminal velocities of the original drop and the smaller droplet is:

$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \dfrac{R^2}{r^2}$

Substituting $R = 4r$:

$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \dfrac{(4r)^2}{r^2} = 16$

Answer: $16$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cylindrical vessel of $40$ cm radius is completely filled with water and its capacity is $528$ dm$^3$ (dm : decimeter). The vessel is placed on a solid block of exactly same height as vessel. If a small hole is made at $70$ cm below the top of water level, then horizontal range of water falling on the ground in the beginning is __________ cm.
questions.solution:
Volume of the cylindrical vessel, $V = 528$ dm$^3 = 528000$ cm$^3$

Radius of the vessel, $r = 40$ cm

Let the height of the vessel be $H$.

$V = \pi r^2 H$

$528000 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times (40)^2 \times H$

$H = \dfrac{528000 \times 7}{22 \times 1600} = 105$ cm

The vessel is placed on a block of height equal to the vessel, so the height of the block is $105$ cm.

Depth of the hole from the top water level, $h = 70$ cm

Height of the hole from the ground, $y = \text{Height of block} + (H - h)$

$y = 105 + (105 - 70) = 140$ cm

Velocity of efflux, $v = \sqrt{2gh}$

Time of flight of water, $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2y}{g}}$

Horizontal range, $R = v \times t = \sqrt{2gh} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2y}{g}} = 2\sqrt{hy}$

$R = 2\sqrt{70 \times 140} = 2\sqrt{70 \times 70 \times 2} = 140\sqrt{2}$ cm

Answer: $140\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Eight mercury drops, each of radius $r$, coalesce to form a bigger drop. The surface energy released in this process is _______. ($S$ is the surface tension of mercury).
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the bigger drop be $R$. Since the total volume remains conserved during the process:

$8 \times \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3$

$R^3 = 8r^3 \Rightarrow R = 2r$

Initial surface energy of the $8$ drops is:

$U_i = 8 \times (4 \pi r^2 S) = 32 \pi r^2 S$

Final surface energy of the bigger drop is:

$U_f = 4 \pi R^2 S = 4 \pi (2r)^2 S = 16 \pi r^2 S$

The surface energy released in the process is:

$\Delta U = U_i - U_f = 32 \pi r^2 S - 16 \pi r^2 S = 16 \pi r^2 S$

Answer: $16\pi r^2 S$

questions.q: A water spray gun is attached to a hose of cross sectional area $30$ cm$^2$. The gun comprises of $10$ perforations each of cross sectional area $15$ mm$^2$. If the water flows in the hose with the speed of $50$ cm/s, calculate the speed at which the water flows out from each perforation. (Neglect any edge effects)
questions.solution:
From the equation of continuity:

$A_1 v_1 = n A_2 v_2$

Here,
$A_1 = 30 \text{ cm}^2 = 30 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$
$v_1 = 50 \text{ cm/s} = 0.5 \text{ m/s}$
$n = 10$
$A_2 = 15 \text{ mm}^2 = 15 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$

Substituting the given values:

$(30 \times 10^{-4}) \times 0.5 = 10 \times (15 \times 10^{-6}) \times v_2$

$15 \times 10^{-4} = 150 \times 10^{-6} \times v_2$

$15 \times 10^{-4} = 1.5 \times 10^{-4} \times v_2$

$v_2 = \dfrac{15 \times 10^{-4}}{1.5 \times 10^{-4}} = 10 \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $10$ m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The surface tension of a soap solution is $3.5 \times 10^{-2}$ N/m. The work required to increase the radius of a soap bubble from $1$ cm to $2$ cm is $\alpha \times 10^{-6}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _____. ($\pi = 22/7$)
questions.solution:
The work done to increase the radius of a soap bubble is given by $W = T \times \Delta A$

Since a soap bubble has two free surfaces, the change in surface area is $\Delta A = 2 \times 4\pi (r_2^2 - r_1^2)$

Substituting the given values:

$W = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 8\pi \times ((2 \times 10^{-2})^2 - (1 \times 10^{-2})^2)$

$W = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 8\pi \times (4 \times 10^{-4} - 1 \times 10^{-4})$

$W = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 8\pi \times 3 \times 10^{-4}$

$W = 84\pi \times 10^{-6}$

Using $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$:

$W = 84 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-6} = 264 \times 10^{-6}$ J

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-6}$ J, we get $\alpha = 264$

Answer: $264$

questions.q: The surface tension of a soap bubble is $0.03$ N/m. The work done in increasing the diameter of bubble from $2$ cm to $6$ cm is $\alpha \pi \times 10^{-4}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. (Take $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
Initial radius $r_1 = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$ cm $= 10^{-2}$ m

Final radius $r_2 = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$ cm $= 3 \times 10^{-2}$ m

Surface tension $T = 0.03$ N/m

A soap bubble has two free surfaces. The change in total surface area is given by:

$\Delta A = 2 \times 4\pi (r_2^2 - r_1^2)$

$\Delta A = 8\pi ((3 \times 10^{-2})^2 - (10^{-2})^2)$

$\Delta A = 8\pi (9 \times 10^{-4} - 10^{-4}) = 64\pi \times 10^{-4}$ m$^2$

Work done $W = T \Delta A$

$W = 0.03 \times 64\pi \times 10^{-4}$

$W = 1.92\pi \times 10^{-4}$ J

Comparing with $\alpha \pi \times 10^{-4}$ J, we get $\alpha = 1.92$.

Answer: $1.92$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If an air bubble of diameter $2$ mm rises steadily through a liquid of density $2000$ kg/m$^3$ at a rate of $0.5$ cm/s, then the coefficient of viscosity of liquid is _______ Poise. (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity of an air bubble rising in a liquid is given by Stokes' law:

$v = \dfrac{2}{9} \dfrac{r^2 \rho g}{\eta}$

Where:
$r = \dfrac{D}{2} = 1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$
$\rho = 2000 \text{ kg/m}^3$
$g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$
$v = 0.5 \text{ cm/s} = 5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m/s}$

Rearranging the formula for the coefficient of viscosity $\eta$:

$\eta = \dfrac{2}{9} \dfrac{r^2 \rho g}{v}$

Substituting the given values:

$\eta = \dfrac{2}{9} \times \dfrac{(10^{-3})^2 \times 2000 \times 10}{5 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\eta = \dfrac{2}{9} \times \dfrac{10^{-6} \times 20000}{5 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\eta = \dfrac{2}{9} \times \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-2}}{5 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\eta = \dfrac{2}{9} \times 4 = \dfrac{8}{9} \text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s}$

To convert the viscosity from SI units (Pa$\cdot$s) to CGS units (Poise), we multiply by $10$:

$\eta = \dfrac{8}{9} \times 10 = \dfrac{80}{9} \text{ Poise}$

$\eta \approx 8.88 \text{ Poise}$

The closest given option is $8.8$.

Answer: $8.8$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A liquid drop of diameter $2$ mm breaks into $512$ droplets. The change in surface energy is $\alpha \times 10^{-6}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. (Take surface tension of liquid $= 0.08$ N/m)
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the initial drop be $R$ and the radius of each small droplet be $r$.

Given diameter $D = 2$ mm, so $R = 1$ mm $= 10^{-3}$ m.

By conservation of volume:

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 512 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

$R^3 = 512 r^3 \Rightarrow R = 8r \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{8}$

Initial surface area, $A_i = 4\pi R^2$

Final surface area, $A_f = 512 \times 4\pi r^2 = 512 \times 4\pi \left(\dfrac{R}{8}\right)^2 = 32\pi R^2$

Change in surface area, $\Delta A = A_f - A_i = 32\pi R^2 - 4\pi R^2 = 28\pi R^2$

Change in surface energy, $\Delta U = T \Delta A$

$\Delta U = 0.08 \times 28\pi R^2$

Substituting $R = 10^{-3}$ m and $\pi \approx \dfrac{22}{7}$:

$\Delta U = 0.08 \times 28 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (10^{-3})^2$

$\Delta U = 0.08 \times 4 \times 22 \times 10^{-6}$

$\Delta U = 7.04 \times 10^{-6}$ J

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-6}$ J, we get $\alpha \approx 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A tub is filled with water and a wooden cube $10$ cm $\times$10$ cm $\times$10$ cm is placed in the water. The wooden cube is found to float on the water with a part of it submerged in water. When a metal coin is placed on the wooden cube, the submerged part is increased by $3.87$ cm. The mass of the metal coin is _______ gram.
(Take water density as $1$ g/cm$^3$ and density of wood as $0.4$ g/cm$^3$)
questions.solution:
Let $A$ be the base area of the wooden cube.

$A = 10 \text{ cm} \times 10 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ cm}^2$

Let $\Delta x$ be the increase in the submerged depth of the cube when the coin is placed on it.

$\Delta x = 3.87 \text{ cm}$

The additional volume of water displaced due to the weight of the metal coin is $\Delta V = A \times \Delta x$.

$\Delta V = 100 \times 3.87 = 387 \text{ cm}^3$

By Archimedes' principle, the weight of the metal coin is balanced by the additional buoyant force, which is equal to the weight of the additional water displaced.

$m g = \Delta V \rho_w g$

$m = \Delta V \rho_w$

Substituting the values of $\Delta V$ and the density of water $\rho_w = 1 \text{ g/cm}^3$:

$m = 387 \text{ cm}^3 \times 1 \text{ g/cm}^3 = 387 \text{ g}$

Answer: $387$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cubical block of density $\rho_{b}=600 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ floats in a liquid of density $\rho_{\mathrm{e}}=900 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$. If the height of block is $H=8.0 \mathrm{~cm}$ then height of the submerged part is $\_\_\_\_$ cm.
questions.solution:
For a floating cubical block in equilibrium, the buoyant force equals the weight:
$\rho_e \cdot g \cdot A \cdot h_s = \rho_b \cdot g \cdot A \cdot H$
where $h_s$ is the submerged height.
Simplifying: $h_s = \frac{\rho_b}{\rho_e} \cdot H = \frac{600}{900} \times 8.0 = \frac{2}{3} \times 8.0$
$= 5.33$ cm ≈ 5.3 cm

questions.q: A soap bubble of surface tension $0.04 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ is blown to a diameter of 7 cm. If $(15000-x) \mu \mathrm{J}$ of work is done in blowing it further to make its diameter 14 cm, then the value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$. ($\pi=22 / 7$)
questions.solution:
Soap bubble has two surfaces. Work done: $W = \Delta A \times \sigma$
Initial radius: $r_i = 3.5$ cm = 0.035 m, Final radius: $r_f = 7$ cm = 0.07 m
Change in surface area (both surfaces): $\Delta A = 8\pi(r_f^2 - r_i^2) = 8\pi(0.07^2 - 0.035^2)$
$\Delta A = 8\pi(0.0049 - 0.001225) = 8\pi \times 0.003675 = 0.0294\pi$ m²
$W = 0.0294\pi \times 0.04 = 0.001176\pi$ J = $0.001176 \times \frac{22}{7} = 0.003696$ J = 3696 μJ
Therefore: $x = 15000 - 3696 = 11304$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sixty four rain drops of radius 1 mm each falling down with a terminal velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$ coalesce to form a bigger drop. The terminal velocity of bigger drop is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
At terminal velocity, gravitational force equals Stokes drag: $mg = 6\pi\eta rv$
For a sphere with mass $m = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho$, this gives $v = \frac{2r^2\rho g}{9\eta}$
Therefore, $v \propto r^2$
When 64 drops coalesce: $64 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r_1^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi r_2^3$, so $r_2 = 4r_1$
New terminal velocity: $\frac{v_2}{v_1} = \left(\frac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^2 = 16$
$v_2 = 16 \times 10 = 160$ cm/s

questions.q:
A small metallic sphere of diameter 2 mm and density $10.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$ is dropped in glycerine having viscosity 10 Poise and density $1.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$ respectively. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$. 
($\pi=\frac{22}{7}$ and $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
questions.solution:
Using Stokes' Law for terminal velocity:
$v_t = \frac{2r^2g(\rho_s - \rho_f)}{9\eta}$.
Given: r = 0.1 cm, g = 1000 cm/s², $\rho_s = 10.5$ g/cm³, $\rho_f = 1.5$ g/cm³, η = 10 Poise = 10 g/(cm⋅s).
Substituting:
$v_t = \frac{2 \times (0.1)^2 \times 1000 \times (10.5 - 1.5)}{9 \times 10}$
$= \frac{2 \times 0.01 \times 1000 \times 9}{90}$
$= \frac{180}{90} = 2.0$ cm/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An air bubble of volume $2.9 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of 5 m deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is $17^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, is $\_\_\_\_ \mathrm{cm}^{3}$.
$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right.$, density of water $=10^{3} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}, and $1 atm pressure is $\left.10^{5} \mathrm{~Pa}\right)$
questions.solution:
An air bubble rises through water with initial volume 2.9 cm³ at the bottom. Calculating pressures at both locations:
At bottom (5 m depth): $P_1 = P_{atm} + \rho gh = 10^5 + 10^3(10)(5) = 1.5 \times 10^5$ Pa
At surface: $P_2 = 10^5$ Pa
Initial temperature: $T_1 = 17°C = 290$ K, Final temperature: $T_2 = 27°C = 300$ K
Using ideal gas law: $\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$
$V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{P_1}{P_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 2.9 \times \frac{1.5 \times 10^5}{10^5} \times \frac{300}{290}$
$= 2.9 \times 1.5 \times \frac{30}{29} = 2.9 \times 1.5 \times 1.034 \approx 4.5$ cm³

questions.q: When a part of a straight capillary tube is placed vertically in a liquid, the liquid raises upto certain height $h$. If the inner radius of the capillary tube, density of the liquid and surface tension of the liquid decrease by $1 \%$ each, then the height of the liquid in the tube will change by $\%$.
questions.solution:
Capillary height formula: $h = \frac{2\sigma\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$
When radius, density, and surface tension each decrease by 1%: $r' = 0.99r$, $\rho' = 0.99\rho$, $\sigma' = 0.99\sigma$
New height: $h' = \frac{2(0.99\sigma)\cos\theta}{(0.99\rho) g (0.99r)} = h \cdot \frac{0.99}{0.99 \times 0.99} = h \cdot \frac{1}{0.99} = h \cdot 1.0101...$
Percentage change: $(1.0101 - 1) \times 100 \approx +1.01\%$, which rounds to +1%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Pressure of a fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid.
Statement II: Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to interior, results in surface tension.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
Statement I is false: Fluid pressure exists everywhere in a still fluid, not only on solid surfaces. According to Pascal's principle, pressure at any point in a static fluid acts equally in all directions and throughout the fluid volume.

Statement II is true: Surface tension results from excess potential energy of molecules at the liquid surface. Surface molecules experience net inward attractive forces from interior molecules, creating an imbalance that increases their potential energy and manifests as surface tension acting along the surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spherical body of radius $r$ and density $\sigma$ falls freely through a viscous liquid having density $\rho$ and viscosity $\eta$ and attains a terminal velocity $v_{0}$. Estimated maximum error in the quantity $\eta$ is : (Ignore errors associated with $\sigma, \rho$ and $g$, gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity $v_0$ of a spherical body falling through a viscous liquid is given by Stokes' Law:
$v_0 = \frac{2r^2(\sigma - \rho)g}{9\eta}$
Rearranging the formula to express viscosity $\eta$ in terms of other variables:
$\eta = \frac{2r^2(\sigma - \rho)g}{9v_0}$
Since we are told to ignore errors associated with $\sigma$, $\rho$, and $g$, these quantities along with the numerical factor $\frac{2}{9}$ are treated as constants.
The expression for $\eta$ can be written as $\eta = k \cdot \frac{r^2}{v_0}$, where $k = \frac{2(\sigma - \rho)g}{9}$ is a constant.
Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:
$\ln \eta = \ln k + 2\ln r - \ln v_0$
Differentiating both sides to find the relative error:
$\frac{d\eta}{\eta} = 0 + 2\frac{dr}{r} - \frac{dv_0}{v_0}$
For the estimated maximum fractional error, we take the absolute sum of the individual relative errors:
$\frac{\Delta \eta}{\eta} = 2\frac{\Delta r}{r} + \frac{\Delta v_0}{v_0}$
This matches option (1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$, are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ where $r_{1}>r_{2}$. The measured liquid heights in these tubes are $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid about the lowest point of miniscus]. The heights $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ and surfaces tensions $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ satisfy the relation:
questions.solution:
For capillary rise, the height of liquid in a tube is given by: $h = \frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$, where $T$ is surface tension and $r$ is the tube radius.

For two liquids with equal density and contact angles:
$h_1 = \frac{2T_1\cos\theta}{\rho g r_1}$ and $h_2 = \frac{2T_2\cos\theta}{\rho g r_2}$

Taking the ratio: $\frac{h_1}{h_2} = \frac{T_1}{T_2} \times \frac{r_2}{r_1}$

Since $r_1 > r_2$, we have $\frac{r_2}{r_1} < 1$. The capillary rise is inversely proportional to tube radius, so the smaller radius tube will have greater height. Since the liquids are measured to have heights $h_1$ and $h_2$ with $r_1 > r_2$, and they have the same density, the empirical relation shows that both liquids rise to different heights inversely proportional to their radii. For liquids with the same density measured in different tubes, if the heights and radii satisfy the capillary rise equation, the surface tensions must be equal: $T_1 = T_2$, and $h_1 < h_2$ since $r_1 > r_2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius 6 mm in a viscous fluid is $20 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius 3 mm in the same fluid will be $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
For a sphere in a viscous fluid, terminal velocity is proportional to $r^2$: $v_t \propto r^2$.
For two balls of the same material in the same fluid: $\frac{v_{t1}}{v_{t2}} = \frac{r_1^2}{r_2^2}$.
Given $r_1 = 6$ mm, $v_{t1} = 20$ cm/s, and $r_2 = 3$ mm: $\frac{20}{v_{t2}} = \frac{36}{9} = 4$.
Therefore, $v_{t2} = 5$ cm/s.

questions.q: Water flows through a horizontal tube as shown in the figure. The difference in height between the water columns in vertical tubes is 5 cm and the area of cross-sections at $A$ and $B$ are $6 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ and $3 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ respectively. The rate of flow will be $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{cm}^{3} / \mathrm{s}$. (take $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
questions.solution:
Given: $h = 5$ cm, $A_1 = 6$ cm², $A_2 = 3$ cm², $g = 1000$ cm/s²
By continuity: $A_1v_1 = A_2v_2 \Rightarrow v_2 = 2v_1$
By Bernoulli's equation: $P_1 - P_2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho(v_2^2 - v_1^2)$
Since $P_1 - P_2 = \rho gh$:
$\rho gh = \frac{1}{2}\rho(4v_1^2 - v_1^2) = \frac{3\rho v_1^2}{2}$
$v_1 = \sqrt{\frac{2gh}{3}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 1000 \times 5}{3}} = \frac{100}{\sqrt{3}}$ cm/s
Rate of flow $Q = A_1v_1 = 6 \times \frac{100}{\sqrt{3}} = 200\sqrt{3}$ cm³/s

questions.q: Consider a completely full cylindrical water tank of height 1.6 m and cross-sectional area $0.5 \mathrm{~m}^2$. It has a small hole in its side at a height 90 cm from the bottom. Assume, the cross-sectional area of the hole to be negligibly small as compared to that of the water tank. If a load 50 kg is applied at the top surface of the water in the tank then the velocity of the water coming out at the instant when the hole is opened is : $\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Apply Bernouli equation between points $1 \& 2$
$\begin{aligned}
& P_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2+\rho g h=P_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2+0 \\ & P_0+\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{~A}}+\rho g \frac{70}{100}=P_0+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2 \\ & \frac{5000}{0.5}+10^3 \times 10 \frac{70}{100}=\frac{1}{2} \times 10^3 v_2^2
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& 10^3+10^3 \times 7=\frac{10^3}{2} \mathrm{v}_2^2 \\ & \mathrm{v}_2^2=16 \\ & \mathrm{v}_2=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
As the tank area is large $\mathrm{v}_1$ is negligible compared to $\mathrm{v}_2$

questions.q:
A vessel with square cross-section and height of 6 m is vertically partitioned. A small window of $100 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ with hinged door is fitted at a depth of 3 m in the partition wall. One part of the vessel is filled completely with water and the other side is filled with the liquid having density $1.5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. What force one needs to apply on the hinged door so that it does not get opened ?
(Acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$)
questions.solution: in equilibrium$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{F}_{\text{ext }}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{w}}=\mathrm{F}_{\ell} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{F}_{\text{ext }}=\mathrm{F}_{\ell}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{w}} \\ & =\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\rho_{\ell} \mathrm{gh}\right) \mathrm{A}-\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\rho_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{gh}\right) \mathrm{A} \\ & =\left(\rho_{\ell}-\rho_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \mathrm{ghA} \\ & =(1500-1000) \times 10 \times 3 \times\left(100 \times 10^{-4}\right) \\ & =150 \mathrm{ m}\end{aligned}$

A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water ?
(Given : density of water $=1000 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ )
questions.solution:
Volume of cube inside water
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{\text{ Denslty$ of $cube }}{\text{ Denslty of water }}\right) \times \text{ Volume of cube } \\
& =\frac{\text{ Mass of cube }}{\text{ Denslty of water }} \\
& =\frac{400 \mathrm{gm}}{1 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^3} \\
& =400 \mathrm{ cm}^3
\end{aligned}$
Volume of cube outside water
$\begin{aligned}
& =\text{ Volume$ of $cube }- \text{ Volume of cube inside water } \\
& =1000 \mathrm{ cm}^3-400 \mathrm{ cm}^3 \\
& =600 \mathrm{ cm}^3
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In the experiment for measurement of viscosity ' $\eta$ ' of given liquid with a ball having radius $R$, consider following statements.
A. Graph between terminal velocity V and R will be a parabola.
B. The terminal velocities of different diameter balls are constant for a given liquid.
C. Measurement of terminal velocity is dependent on the temperature.
D. This experiment can be utilized to assess the density of a given liquid.
E. If balls are dropped with some initial speed, the value of $\eta$ will change.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity of ball of radius $R$ inside a liquid of viscosity $\eta$ can be written as $V_T=\frac{2 R^2 g}{n}(\sigma-\rho)$, where $\sigma$ is the density of ball and $\delta$ is the density of the liquid.
Hence,
$A$ is correct since $V_T \propto R^2$ gives a parabola on a graph
$C$ is correct since $V_T \alpha \frac{1}{\eta}$ and $\eta$ varies with temperature
$D$ is correct since $V_T \alpha(\sigma-\rho)$ i.e., varies with density of liquid.

A. Surface tension arises due to extra energy of the molecules at the interior as compared to the molecules at the surface, of a liquid.

C. As the temperature of gas increases, the coefficient of viscosity increases

E. In a steady flow two stream lines never intersect.

questions.solution: Surface tension arises due to extra energy of the molecules at the molecules at the surface as compared at the interior of a liquid. questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & F=m \omega^2 r_{\mathrm{cm}} \\ & r_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \\ & \omega=\sqrt{\frac{2 F}{m}} \\ & m=2 M \\ & \omega=\sqrt{\frac{F}{M}} \\ & \alpha=1\end{aligned}\)$

questions.q: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is thrice the excess pressure inside a second soap bubble. The ratio between the volume of the first and the second bubble is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sphere of relative density $\sigma$ and diameter $D$ has concentric cavity of diameter $d$. The ratio of $\frac{D}{d}$, if it just floats on water in a tank is :
questions.solution:
weight $(w)=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{D}^3-\mathrm{d}^3}{8}\right) \sigma \mathrm{g}$
Buoyant force $\left(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}}\right)=1 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{D}^3}{8}\right) \cdot \mathrm{g}$
For Just Float $\Rightarrow \mathrm{w}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}} \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(D^3-d^3\right) \sigma=D^3 \\ & \Rightarrow 1-\frac{d^3}{D^3}=\frac{1}{\sigma} \\ & \Rightarrow 1-\frac{1}{\sigma}=\left(\frac{d}{D}\right)^3 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{\sigma}{\sigma-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}=\left(\frac{D}{d}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A cube of ice floats partly in water and partly in kerosene oil. The ratio of volume of ice immersed in water to that in kerosene oil (specific gravity of Kerosene oil $=0.8$, specific gravity of ice $=0.9$)
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}_1=\text{ volume immersed$ in $water. } \\ & \mathrm{v}_2=\text{ volume immersed in oil. } \\ & \mathrm{v}_1 \rho_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{g}+\mathrm{v}_2 \rho_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{g}=\left(\mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{v}_2\right) \rho_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{g} \\ & \mathrm{v}_1+\frac{\mathrm{v}_2 \rho_{\mathrm{o}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{w}}}=\left(\mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{v}_2\right) \frac{\rho_{\mathrm{c}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{w}}} \\ & =\mathrm{v}_1+0.8 \mathrm{v}_2=0.9 \mathrm{v}_1+0.9 \mathrm{v}_2 \\ & =0.1 \mathrm{v}_1=0.1 \mathrm{v}_2 \\ & \mathrm{v}_1: \mathrm{v}_2=1: 1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Small water droplets of radius $0.01 \mathrm{~mm}$ are formed in the upper atmosphere and falling with a terminal velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Due to condensation, if 8 such droplets are coalesced and formed a larger drop, the new terminal velocity will be _____$\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{m}=$ mass of small drop
$\mathrm{M}=$ mass of bigger drop
$\begin{aligned} & V_t=\frac{2}{9} \frac{R^2(\rho-\sigma) g}{\eta} \\ & 8 \propto m=M \\ & 8 r^3=R^3 \Rightarrow R=2 R\end{aligned}$
as $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}} \times \mathrm{R}^2 \quad \because$ Radius double so $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}}$ becomes 4 time
$\therefore 4 \times 10=40 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.q: A small ball of mass $m$ and density $\rho$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density $\rho_0$. After sometime, the ball falls with constant velocity. The viscous force on the ball is :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{ma} \mathrm{a}=0$ for constant velocity
$\begin{aligned}
& m g-F_B=F_v \\

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small droplets of water. The ratio of surface energy of 1000 droplets to that of energy of big drop is $\frac{10}{x}$. The value of $x$ is __________
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} 1000 \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 & =\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \\ 10 r & =R \\ R & =10 r\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} \frac{\text{ S.E.$ of $} 1000 \text{ drops }}{\text{ S.E. of Big drop }} & =\frac{1000\left(4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2\right) \mathrm{T}}{4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{ T}} \\ & =\frac{1000 \times \mathrm{r}^2}{(10 \mathrm{r})^2}=10=\frac{10}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \therefore \quad x & =1\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: Statement I : When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation $P_1-P_2=\rho g\left(h_2-h_1\right)$. Statement II : In ventury tube shown $2 \mathrm{gh}=v_1^2-v_2^2$
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation $\mathrm{P}_1+\rho \mathrm{gh}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\rho \mathrm{gh}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2 \left[h_1 \& h_2\right.$ are height of point from any reference level] Given $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2=0$ (for statement-1) $\therefore \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_2=\mathrm{g}\left(\mathrm{h}_2-\mathrm{h}_2\right)$
For statement-2 $\mathrm{P}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2 \begin{aligned} & P_1-P_2=\rho g h \\ & P_1-P_2=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & \rho g h=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & 2 g h=v_2^2-v_1^2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A plane is in level flight at constant speed and each of its two wings has an area of $40{m}^{2} .$ If the speed of the air is $180km{h}^{- 1}$ over the lower wing surface and $252km{h}^{- 1}$ over the upper wing surface, the mass of the plane is ________$kg .$ (Take air density to be $1kg{m}^{– 3}$ and $g = 10m{s}^{– 2}$)

Total wing span area, $A = 2 \times 40 = 80{m}^{2}$

$A\left({P}_{2} - {P}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({V}_{1}^{2} - {V}_{2}^{2}\right)A$

$⇒ mg = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1\left({70}^{2} - {50}^{2}\right) \times 80$

questions.q: A small liquid drop of radius $R$ is divided into $27$ identical liquid drops. If the surface tension is $T$, then the work done in the process will be :
questions.solution:
Let radius of the newly formed drops be $r$.

As total volume will remain constant, therefore

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} = 27 \times \left(\dfrac{4}{3} \times \pi{r}^{3}\right)$

$⇒ {R}^{3} = 27{r}^{3}$

$⇒ R = 3r$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{3}$

$⇒ {r}^{2} = \dfrac{{R}^{2}}{9}$

Now, work done $= T \times \DeltaA$

$= T\left[27\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right)\right] - T\left[4\pi{R}^{2}\right] = T\left[27\left(4\pi\dfrac{{R}^{2}}{9}\right)\right] - T\left[4\pi{R}^{2}\right] = T\pi{R}^{2}\left(12 - 4\right)$

$= 8\pi{R}^{2}T$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water.
Statement II : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in cold water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
For water, the surface tension decreases as the temperature increases. At higher temperatures, the water molecules have more kinetic energy and are better able to overcome the cohesive forces at the surface, resulting in a decrease in surface tension.

So, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water and larger in cold water.

Hence, statement I is true, but statement II is false.

questions.q: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are $70m{s}^{- 1}$ and $65m{s}^{- 1}$ respectively. If the wing area is $2{m}^{2}$, the lift of the wing is _______$N$. (Given density of air $= 1 . 2kg{m}^{- 3}$)
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's principle on upper & lower surfaces, we get

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{2}\right)}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2}$

Since, height difference between upper and lower surface is negligible.

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{\left({v}_{2}\right)}^{2}$

Therefore, upthrust acting due to pressure difference:

$⇒ \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({v}_{1}^{2} - {v}_{2}^{2}\right) ⇒ F = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 . 2 \times \left({70}^{2} - {65}^{2}\right) \times 2$

$= 810N$

questions.q: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is $4 . 5 \times {10}^{4}N{m}^{- 2}$. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to $2 . 0 \times {10}^{4}N{m}^{- 2}$. The velocity of water is found to be $\sqrt{V}m{s}^{- 1}$. The value of $V$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the change in pressure can be written as

${P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

$4 . 5 \times {10}^{4} - 2 . 0 \times {10}^{4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2} ⇒ 2 . 5 \times {10}^{4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2} ⇒ {v}^{2} = 50 ⇒ v = \sqrt{50}$

Hence, $V = 50$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : Viscosity of gases is greater than that of liquids.

Statement (II) : Surface tension of a liquid decreases due to the presence of insoluble impurities.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.solution:
Viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow, and gases typically have lower molecular interactions and are less dense than liquids, resulting in lower viscosity.

The presence of insoluble impurities in a liquid can decrease its surface tension. Surface tension is related to the cohesive forces between molecules at the surface of a liquid. Insoluble impurities can disrupt these cohesive forces, leading to a decrease in surface tension.

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: There is an air bubble of radius $1 . 0mm$ in a liquid of surface tension $0 . 075N{m}^{– 1}$ and density $1000kg{m}^{– 3}$ at a depth of $10cm$ below the free surface. The amount by which the pressure inside the bubble is greater than the atmospheric pressure is _______ $Pa\left(g = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right)$.
questions.solution:
The pressure inside the bubble is given by

$\DeltaP = P - {P}_{0} = ρgh + \dfrac{2T}{r}$

The data given is

$r = {10}^{- 3}mT = 0 . 075N{m}^{- 1}ρ = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}h = 10cm$

Therefore, the pressure in the bubble is

$\DeltaP = \left(1000 \times 10 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) + \dfrac{2 \times 0 . 075}{{10}^{- 3}} = 1000 + 150 = 1150Pa$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as

Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : A spherical body of radius $( 5 \pm 0 . 1 ) mm$ having a particular density is falling through a liquid of constant density. The percentage error in the calculation of its terminal velocity is $4 %$.

Reason R : The terminal velocity of the spherical body falling through the liquid is inversely proportional to its radius. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity is

${V}_{T} = \dfrac{2}{9}{r}^{2}g\dfrac{\left(ρ - {ρ}^{'}\right)}{η} ⇒ {V}_{T} ∝ {r}^{2}$

Differentiating and dividing by ${V}_{T}$,

$⇒ \dfrac{d{V}_{T}}{{V}_{T}} = 2\dfrac{dr}{r} = 2 \times \dfrac{0 . 1}{5}$

So, the percentage error is

$\dfrac{d{V}_{T}}{{V}_{T}} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 2}{5} \times 100 = 4 %$

As can be seen the terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of the radius. Hence $A$ is true but $R$ is false.

The figure shows a liquid of given density flowing steadily in horizontal tube of varying cross-section. Cross-sectional areas at $A$ is $1 . 5{cm}^{2},$ and $B$ is $25{mm}^{2},$ if the speed of liquid at $B$ is $60cm{s}^{- 1}$ then $( {P}_{A} – {P}_{B} )$ is

(Given ${P}_{A}$ and ${P}_{B}$ are liquid pressures at $A$ and $B$ points.

Density $ρ = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$

$A$ and $B$ are on the axis of tube)
questions.solution:
Using Bernoulli's theorem,

${P}_{A} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{A}^{2} = {P}_{B} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{B}^{2} . . . ( i )$

Using equation of continuity,

${A}_{A}{V}_{A} = {A}_{B}{V}_{B}$

So, $1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4} \times {V}_{A} = 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {V}_{B}$

${V}_{A} = \dfrac{25 \times {10}^{- 6}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} \times 0 . 6$

$= \dfrac{1}{10}m{s}^{- 1}$

Substituting in equation (i)

$⇒ {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \dfrac{1000}{2}\left[0 . {6}^{2} - 0 . {1}^{2}\right] = \dfrac{1000}{2} \times 0 . 7 \times 0 . 5$

$= 175Pa$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $64$ identical drops each charged upto potential of $10mV$ are combined to form a bigger drop. The potential of the bigger drop will be _____ $mV$.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the potential $\left(V\right)$ of each tiny drop is given by

$V = k\dfrac{q}{r} . . . \left(1\right)$

When all the drops forms the bigger drop the radius of the new drop $\left(r '\right)$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}Volumeofbigdrop & = & 64 \times volumeofeachtinydrop \\ ⇒ & \dfrac{4}{3}\pir{'}^{3} = 64 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} \\ ⇒ & r ' = 4r\end{cases}$

So, the potential of the new big drop $\left(V '\right)$ can be written as

$\begin{cases}V ' & = & k\dfrac{64q}{r '} \\ = & k\dfrac{64q}{4r} \\ = & 16k\dfrac{q}{r} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the potential of the new drop.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{V '}{V} & = & \dfrac{16k\dfrac{q}{r}}{k\dfrac{q}{r}} \\ ⇒ & V ' = 16V . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required value of the potential for the new drop.

$\begin{cases}V ' & = & 16 \times 10mV \\ = & 160mV\end{cases}$

questions.q: Glycerin of density $1 . 25 \times {10}^{3}kg{m}^{– 3}$ is flowing through the conical section of pipe. The area of cross-section of the pipe at its ends are $10{cm}^{2}$ and $5{cm}^{2}$ and pressure drop across its length is $3N{m}^{– 2}$. The rate of flow of glycerine through the pipe is $x \times {10}^{– 5}{m}^{3}{s}^{– 1}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
It is given that

${A}_{1} = 10{cm}^{2}; {A}_{2} = 5{cm}^{2}$

$∆ P = 3N{m}^{- 2}$

By continuity equation,

${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2} ⇒ {v}_{1} = \dfrac{{A}_{2}{v}_{2}}{{A}_{1}} . . . ( i )$

By Bernoulli's equation,

$\dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{2}}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{1}}^{2} = ∆ P . . . ( ii )$

Using equation (i) in (ii)

$∆ P = \dfrac{ρ}{2} ( {v}^{2}2 - {\left(\dfrac{{A}_{2}{v}_{2}}{{A}_{1}}\right)}^{2} ) ⇒ ∆ P = \dfrac{ρ{v}^{2}2}{2}\left(1 - {\left(\dfrac{{A}_{2}}{{A}_{1}}\right)}^{2}\right) ⇒ 3 = \dfrac{1 . 25 \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2}2}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) ⇒ {v}^{2}2 = \dfrac{6 \times 4}{1 . 25 \times {10}^{3} \times 3} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 8 \times {10}^{- 2}m{s}^{- 1}$

So, the discharge rate is,

${A}_{2}{v}_{2} = x \times {10}^{- 5} ⇒ x = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 8 \times {10}^{- 2}}{{10}^{- 5}} = 4$

By Bernoulli's equation,

$\dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{2}}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{1}}^{2} = ∆ P . . . ( ii )$

Using equation (i) in (ii)

$∆ P = \dfrac{ρ}{2} ( {v}^{2}2 - {\left(\dfrac{{A}_{2}{v}_{2}}{{A}_{1}}\right)}^{2} ) ⇒ ∆ P = \dfrac{ρ{v}^{2}2}{2}\left(1 - {\left(\dfrac{{A}_{2}}{{A}_{1}}\right)}^{2}\right) ⇒ 3 = \dfrac{1 . 25 \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2}2}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) ⇒ {v}^{2}2 = \dfrac{6 \times 4}{1 . 25 \times {10}^{3} \times 3} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 8 \times {10}^{- 2}m{s}^{- 1}$

So, the discharge rate is,

${A}_{2}{v}_{2} = x \times {10}^{- 5} ⇒ x = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 8 \times {10}^{- 2}}{{10}^{- 5}} = 4$

questions.q: Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady speed of $10cm{s}^{- 1}$. If the drops coalesce, the new velocity is:-
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity can be given by

${v}_{T} = \dfrac{2 ( ρ - \sigma ) {r}^{2}g}{9η}$.

Clearly, ${v}_{T} ∝ {r}^{2}$

Let the radius of the small drops be ${r}_{1}$ and the radius of the big drop be ${r}_{2}$.

So,

$8\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right){r}_{1}^{3} = \left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right){r}_{2}^{3} ⇒ {r}_{1} = \dfrac{{r}_{2}}{2}$

Hence, taking the ratio
$\dfrac{{\left({v}_{T}\right)}_{1}}{{\left({v}_{T}\right)}_{2}} = {\left(\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}}\right)}^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{10}{{\left({v}_{T}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$⇒ {\left({v}_{T}\right)}_{2} = 40cm{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: The surface tension of soap solution is  $3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}N{m}^{- 1}$. The amount of work done required to increase the radius of soap bubble from $10cm$ to $20cm$ is _____$\times {10}^{- 4}J$ . (take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution:
The amount of work done is equal to the change in the surface energy to increase the radius of the bubble.

The formula to calculate the change in surface energy is given by

$\DeltaU = 2 ( T \times \DeltaA ) . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required work done.

$\begin{cases}∆ U & = & 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 4\pi\left[( 0 . 2{)}^{2} - ( 0 . 1{)}^{2}\right] \times 2J \\ = & 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0 . 03 \times 2 \\ = & 2 \times 1 . 32 \times {10}^{- 2} \\ = & 264 \times {10}^{- 4}J\end{cases}$

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pressure in a reservoir of water is same at all points at the same level of water.

Statement II: The pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted in all directions equally.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true

questions.solution:
Pressure in a static fluid will be same at each point on same horizontal level.

$P = {P}_{0} + ρgh$

where ${P}_{0}$ is atmospheric pressure.

Pascal's law states that pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted equally in all directions. Hence, both the statements are true and this is the right option.

questions.q: An air bubble of volume $1{cm}^{3}$ rises from the bottom of a lake $40m$ deep to the surface at a temperature of $12 ° C .$ The atmospheric pressure is  $1 \times {10}^{5}Pa,$ the density of water is $1000kg{m}^{- 3}$ and $g = 10m{s}^{- 2} .$There is no difference of the temperature of water at the depth of $40m$ and on the surface. The volume of air bubble when it reaches the surface will be
questions.solution:
The pressure at the bottom of the lake can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{P}_{bottom} & = & {P}_{0} + ρgh \\ & = & \left({10}^{5} + 1000 \times 10 \times 40\right)Pa \\ & = & 5 \times {10}^{5}Pa\end{cases}$

${P}_{bottom}{V}_{bottom} = {P}_{top}{V}_{top} . . . ( 1 )$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface.

$\begin{cases}5 \times {10}^{5} \times 1 & = & 1 \times {10}^{5} \times {V}_{top} \\ & ⇒ & {V}_{top} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{5} \times 1}{1 \times {10}^{5}}{cm}^{3} \\ & = & 5{cm}^{3}\end{cases}$

questions.solution:
The bubble is moving with a constant velocity so the net force acting on the body is zero.

Stokes' law defines the drag force which is given by $F = 6\piηrv$

The buoyant force is given by $B = Vρg = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3}ρg$

Hence, it can be written that

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3}ρg = 6\piηrv ⇒ η = \dfrac{2{r}^{2}ρg}{9v} = \dfrac{2 \times {\left(3 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2} \times 1750 \times 10}{9 \times 0 . 35 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 10Pas$

Assertion A: When you squeeze one end of a tube to get toothpaste out from the other end, Pascal’s principle is observed.

Reason R: A change in the pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and to the walls of its container.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R is correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.solution:
Pascal's law states that the pressure in a closed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

The formula for pressure is given by

$P = \dfrac{F}{A}$

When a toothpaste is squeezed let the pressure transmitted by $P$. At the mouth of the toothpaste the pressure will also be equal to $P$ due to Pascal's law. The pressure applied to the tube is transmitted equally throughout the toothpaste. When the pressure reaches the open end, it forces toothpaste out through the opening. Hence, both $A \text{ and } R$ is correct and $R$ is correct explanation for $A$.

questions.q: A small ball of mass $M$ and density $ρ$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density ${ρ}_{0}$. After some time, the ball falls with a constant velocity. What is the viscous force on the ball?
questions.solution:
The buoyant force is given by

$B = V{ρ}_{0}g$

where $V$ is the volume of the ball. The weight of the ball

$W = Mg = Vρg$, is acting in the opposite direction of the buoyant force . Hence, at terminal velocity

$Mg - B = {F}_{v}$

$⇒ B + {F}_{v} = Mg$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = Vρg - V{ρ}_{0}g ⇒ {F}_{v} = ρVg ( 1 - \dfrac{{ρ}_{0}}{ρ} ) ⇒ {F}_{v} = Mg ( 1 - \dfrac{{ρ}_{0}}{ρ} )$

questions.q: A mercury drop of radius ${10}^{– 3}m$ is broken into $125$ equal size droplets. Surface tension of mercury is $0 . 45N{m}^{– 1}$ . The gain in surface energy is:

As the volume of the mercury will remain same, therefore

$= 4 \times 0 . 45 \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 6}$

$= 2 . 26 \times {10}^{- 5}J$

questions.q:
If $1000$ droplets of water of surface tension $0 . 07N{m}^{- 1}$. having same radius $1mm$ each, combine to from a single drop. In the process the released surface energy is-

$\left(\text{Take}\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution:
Let the radius of bigger droplet is $R$, then by volume conservation:

$\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}\right) = 1000\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{\left(1\right)}^{3}\right)$

$⇒ R = 10mm$

Final potential energy:

${U}_{f} = 1000\left(4\pi{R}^{2}T\right) = 1000 \times 4\pi{\left(10 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}T$

Initial potential energy:

${U}_{i} = 4\pi \times {\left(r\right)}^{2}T = 4\pi \times {\left({10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}T$

Therefore, change in potential energy,

$∆ E = T \times 1000 \times 4\pi{\left({10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2} - T \times 4\pi{\left(10 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}$

$∆ E = 4 \times \pi \times 7 \times {10}^{- 2}\left[1000 - 100\right] \times {10}^{- 6}$

$∆ E = 7 . 92 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A fully loaded boeing aircraft has a mass of $5 . 4 \times {10}^{5}kg$. Its total wing area is $500{m}^{2}$. It is in level flight with a speed of $1080km{h}^{- 1}$. If the density of air $ρ$ is $1 . 2kg{m}^{– 3}$, the fractional increase in the speed of the air on the upper surface of the wing relative to the lower surface in percentage will be

($g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Required lift force, $F = {P}_{2}A - {P}_{1}A = 5 . 4 \times {10}^{5} \times g$

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{5 . 4 \times {10}^{6}}{500} = 5 . 4 \times 2 \times {10}^{3}$

$= 10 . 8 \times {10}^{3}$

Now applying Bernoulli's Theorem we get

${P}_{2} + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{2}^{2} = {P}_{1} + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({V}_{1}^{2} - {V}_{2}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)\left({V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right)\left[\text{Since$ for $small change}, {V}_{1} = {V}_{2} = V = 1080km{h}^{- 1} = 300m{s}^{- 1}\right]$

$⇒ 10 . 8 \times {10}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 . 2\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right) \times 2 \times 300$

$⇒ 10 . 8 \times 10 = 3 . 6\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ {V}_{1} - {V}_{2} = 30$

Therefore, fractional increase will be$\left(\dfrac{{V}_{1} - {V}_{2}}{V}\right) \times 100 = \dfrac{30}{300} \times 100 = 10 %$

If the viscosity of the liquid is $5 . 0 \times {10}^{– 3}Pl$, the speed of block is ______ $\times {10}^{- 3}m{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
Viscous force is given by,

$| F | = ηA\dfrac{\Deltav}{\Deltah}$

$⇒ 0 . 1 = 5 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 2 \times \dfrac{v}{0 . 25 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$⇒ v = 0 . 025m{s}^{- 1}$

$⇒ v = 25 \times {10}^{- 3}m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: Surface tension of a soap bubble is $2 . 0 \times {10}^{- 2}N{m}^{- 1}$ . Work done to increase the radius of soap bubble from $3 . 5cm$ to $7cm$ will be : [Take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$ ]
questions.solution:
As we know,

Work done $=$ change in surface energy of soap bubble

Therefore,

Work done $= 2T\left(4\pi{r}_{2}^{2} - 4\pi{r}_{1}^{2}\right)$

$= 8\piT\left({r}_{2}^{2} - {r}_{1}^{2}\right)$

$= 8 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0 . 02\left({7}^{2} - 3 . {5}^{2}\right) \times {10}^{- 4}J$

$= 18 . 48 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

questions.q: A spherical drop of liquid splits into $1000$ identical spherical drops. If ${u}_{i}$ is the surface energy of the original drop and ${u}_{f}$ is the total surface energy of the resulting drops, the (ignoring evaporation), $\dfrac{{u}_{f}}{{u}_{i}} = \left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)$. Then value of $x$ is ______:
questions.solution:
Let $R$ be the radius of bigger drop and $r$ be the radius of smaller drop.

Here, volume will remain conserved, so ${V}_{R} = {V}_{r}$.

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} = 1000 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3}$

$⇒ R = 10r$

As surface energy is stated as $u = SA$, here, $S$ is surface tension and $A$ is surface area.

Thus, ${u}_{i} = S\left(4\pi{R}^{2}\right)$ and ${u}_{f} = S\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right) \times 1000$

The ratio is $\dfrac{{u}_{f}}{{u}_{i}} = \dfrac{1000{r}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{u}_{f}}{{u}_{i}} = \dfrac{10}{1}$

Hence, the value of $x = 1$.

questions.q:
A spherical ball of radius $1mm$ and density $10 . 5g{cc}^{- 1}$ is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity $9 . 8$ poise and density $1 . 5g{cc}^{- 1}$. Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is $3696 \times {10}^{- x}N$. The value of $x$ is

(Given, $g = 9 . 8m{s}^{- 2}\text{and}\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution:
Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity i.e., terminal velocity is,

${F}_{v} = \left(mg - {F}_{B}\right)\left(\text{As}, a = 0\right)$

Here, ${F}_{B}$ is buoyant force.

$⇒ {F}_{v} = V{ρ}_{b}g - V{ρ}_{g}g = Vg\left({ρ}_{b} - {ρ}_{g}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{\left({10}^{- 3}\right)}^{3} \times 9 . 8\left[\left(10 . 5 - 1 . 5\right) \times {10}^{3}\right] \approx 3696 \times {10}^{- 7}N$

Thus, $x = 7$.

questions.q:
The velocity of a small ball of mass $0 . 3g$ and density $8g{cc}^{- 1}$ when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is $1 . 3g{cc}^{- 1}$, then the value of viscous force acting on the ball will be $x \times {10}^{- 4}N$, the value of $x$ is _____ .

[use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Let ${F}_{V}$ be the viscous force and ${F}_{B}$ be the buoyant force acting on the ball.

​​​​​​​

Then, when body moves with constant velocity,

${F}_{V} + {F}_{B} = Mg$

Or, ${F}_{V} = Mg - {F}_{B}$

${F}_{V} = {ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{L}Vg$= \left({ρ}_{B} -\right)\left({ρ}_{L}\right)Vg$, where, $V$ is the volume of small ball.

$= \left(8 - 1 . 3\right) × {10}^{3} × \dfrac{0 . 3 × {10}^{- 3}}{8 × {10}^{3}} × 10$

$= \dfrac{6 . 7 × 0 . 3}{8} × {10}^{- 2}$

$= \dfrac{67 × 3}{8} × {10}^{- 4} = 25 . 125 × {10}^{- 4} = 25 × {10}^{- 4}N$

Thus, the value of $x = 25$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Clothes containing oil or grease stains cannot be cleaned by water wash.

Reason (R) : Because the angle of contact between the oil/ grease and water is obtuse. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Angle of contact between oil and water is obtuse i.e., greater than critical angle of contact $\left(\thetac > 90 °\right)$, therefore they do not stick and that's the reason grease/oil stains can not be removed by water wash.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pressure-pump has a horizontal tube of cross-sectional area $10{cm}^{2}$ for the outflow of water at a speed of $20m{s}^{- 1}$. The force exerted on the vertical wall just in front of the tube which stops water horizontally flowing out of the tube, is: [given : density of water $= 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$]
questions.solution:
Volume of water coming out of the pipe per sec $= Av = 10 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 20 = 0 . 02{m}^{3}{s}^{- 1}$

Mass of water hitting the wall per second $m = 0 . 02 \times {10}^{3} = 20kg{s}^{- 1}$

As the water hits the wall normal to the wall and stops, the change of momentum of water hitting the wall is $= m\left(0 - \left(- v\right)\right) = mv$

$= 20 \times 20 = 400kgm{s}^{- 2}$

Since, the change of momentum obtained is per unit time, it is same as the force.

Thus, the force acting on the wall by water $=$ force experienced by water jet$= 400N$.

questions.q:
Consider a cylindrical tank of radius $1m$ is filled with water. The top surface of water is at $15m$ from the bottom of the cylinder. There is a hole on the wall of cylinder at a height of $5m$ from the bottom. A force of $5 × {10}^{5}N$ is applied an the top surface of water using a piston. The speed of efflux from the hole will be :
(given atmospheric pressure ${P}_{A} = 1 . 01 × {10}^{5}Pa$, density of water ${ρ}_{w} = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Assuming there is no atmospheric pressure on piston, ${P}_{1} = \dfrac{F}{\pi{R}^{2}}$ and ${P}_{2} = {P}_{0}$.

Applying Bernoulli's equation at point $1$ and $2$,

${p}_{1} + ρg{h}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{1}^{2} = {p}_{2} + ρg{h}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{F}{\pi{R}^{2}}\right) + ρg\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right) = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2F}{\pi{R}^{2}ρ} - \dfrac{2{P}_{0}}{ρ} + 2g\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right)}$

${v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times \left(5 \times {10}^{5}\right)}{3 . 14 \times {1}^{2} \times 1000} - \dfrac{2 \times 1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}}{1000} + 2 \times 10 \times 10}$

$\approx 17 . 8m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: The diameter of an air bubble which was initially $2mm$, rises steadily through a solution of density $1750 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ at the rate of $0.35 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Coefficient of viscosity of the solution is ______ (Assume mass of the bubble to be negligible) (Answer in Poise to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
As the bubble is rising steadily the net force acting on it will be zero.

(Because of density of air is negligible, so the value of $mg$ can be neglected)

So, the force of buoyancy $B$ is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid acting upward is equal to the viscous force acting downward, i.e., $B = F$.

$⇒ \dfrac{4\pi}{3}{R}^{3}ρg = 6\piηRv$

Putting $R = 1mm = {10}^{- 3}m$, $ρ = 1 . 75 \times {10}^{3}kg{m}^{- 3}$, g = 10m{s}^{- 2} and $v = 0 . 35 \times {10}^{- 2}m{s}^{- 1}$

$η = \dfrac{10}{9} = 1 \cdot 11$

In SI unit, $η = 11$ poise $\left(CGS\right)$.

questions.q: A spherical soap bubble of radius $3cm$ is formed inside another spherical soap bubble of radius $6cm$. If the internal pressure of the smaller bubble of radius $3cm$ in the above system is equal to the internal pressure of the another single soap bubble of radius $rcm$. The value of $r$ is _____
questions.solution:
Pressure inside a bubble is given by, ${P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{r}$.

Pressure inside the bubble of smaller radius will be,

${P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \left[\left({P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{6}\right) + \dfrac{4T}{3}\right]$

Pressure inside the bubble with radius $r$, ${P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{r}$

Now,

$⇒ {P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{6} + \dfrac{4T}{3} = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{r}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ r = 2cm$

questions.q: Two cylindrical vessels of equal cross-sectional area $16{cm}^{2}$ contain water upto heights $100cm$ and $150cm$ respectively. The vessels are interconnected so that the water levels in them become equal. The work done by the force of gravity during the process, is [Take density of water $= {10}^{3}kg{m}^{- 3}$ and $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Initially, the centre of mass of the right column will be at height of $75cm$ and the centre of mass of the left column will be at $50cm$. After opening of the valve both columns will have height of $125cm$ and their centre of mass will be at height $\dfrac{125}{2}cm$. Therefore,

$W = - ∆ U = - \left[\left({m}_{1} + {m}_{2}\right)g\dfrac{{h}_{1} + {h}_{2}}{4} - {m}_{1}g\dfrac{{h}_{1}}{2} - {m}_{2}g\dfrac{{h}_{2}}{2}\right]$

Now, ${m}_{1} = ρA{h}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2} = ρA{h}_{2}$

Putting $ρ = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}, g = 10m{s}^{- 2}, {h}_{1} = 100cm, {h}_{2} = 150cm$ and $A = 16 \times {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}$, we get,

$W = 1J$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A water drop of radius $1cm$ is broken into $729$ equal droplets. If surface tension of water is $75dyne{cm}^{- 1}$, then the gain in surface energy upto first decimal place will be

[Given $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.solution:
The volume of the bigger drop will be, $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$. If the radius of smaller drops is $r$, using the conservation of volume,

$n\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} ⇒ 729 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} ⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{9}$

The initial surface energy will be,

${E}_{i} = \left(4\pi{R}^{2}\right)T$

And final surface energy will be,

${E}_{f} = n\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right)T = 729 \times 4\pi{\left(\dfrac{R}{9}\right)}^{2}T$= 36\pi{R}^{2}T$

Therefore, the change in the surface energy will be,

$⇒ \DeltaE = {E}_{f} - {E}_{i} = 32\pi{R}^{2}T = 32 \times 3 . 14 \times {\left(1 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2} \times 75 \times {10}^{- 3} ⇒ \DeltaE = 7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

questions.q: A drop of liquid of density $ρ$ is floating half immersed in a liquid of density $\sigma$ and surface tension $7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}N{cm}^{- 1}$. The radius of drop in $cm$ will be : (Take : $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Balancing the forces on drop

Buoyant force $+$ surface tension $= mg$

$\sigma\dfrac{V}{2}g + 2\piRT = ρVg$

$2\piRT = \dfrac{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)}{2} \cdot \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}g; \left[\text{As}V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}\right]$

$⇒ {R}^{3} = \dfrac{3T}{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)g} ⇒ R = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}N - {m}^{- 1}}{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right) \times 10}}$

$R = \dfrac{3}{20\sqrt{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)}}m = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2ρ - \sigma}}cm$

$⇒ {R}^{3} = \dfrac{3T}{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)g} ⇒ R = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}N - {m}^{- 1}}{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right) \times 10}}$

$R = \dfrac{3}{20\sqrt{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)}}m = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2ρ - \sigma}}cm$

questions.q: A small spherical ball of radius $0 . 1mm$ and density ${10}^{4}kg{m}^{- 3}$ falls freely under gravity through a distance $h$ before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of $h$ will be ____ $m$. (Given $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$, viscosity of water $= 1 . 0 \times {10}^{- 5}N ‐ s{m}^{- 2}$ ).
questions.solution:
Using equation of motion, ${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$

${v}^{2} = 0 + 2\left(- g\right)\left(- h\right)$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = 2gh$

Initial velocity of ball is $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{20h}$.

If after entering the water this velocity does not change, then this value should be equal to the terminal velocity.

Then, $\sqrt{2gh} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{r}^{2}\left(ρ - \sigma\right)g}{η}$, here, $ρ$ is density of ball, $\sigma$ is density of water and $η$ is viscosity.

$⇒ \sqrt{20h} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{\left(0 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}\left({10}^{4} - {10}^{3}\right)10}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}} ⇒ \sqrt{20h} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{10}^{- 8}\left(10 - 1\right){10}^{3} \times 10}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}}$

$⇒ 20h = 400$

$∴ h = 20m$

questions.q: A liquid of density $750kg{m}^{- 3}$ flows smoothly through a horizontal pipe that tapers in cross-sectional area from ${A}_{1} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}{m}^{2}$ to ${A}_{2} = \dfrac{{A}_{1}}{2}$. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of the pipe is $4500Pa$. The rate of flow of liquid is _____ $\times {10}^{- 3}{m}^{3}{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
From the equation of continuity, ${v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$.

Applying the Bernoulli's Theorem,

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{ρ{{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{ρ4{\left({v}_{1}\right)}^{2}}{2}$⇒ {P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = \dfrac{3ρ{{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ 4500 = \dfrac{3 \times 750 \times {{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2} ⇒ {v}_{1} = 2m{s}^{- 1}$

Now volume flow rate,$Q = A{v}_{1} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 2 = 24 \times {10}^{- 3}{m}^{3}{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A water drop of diameter $2cm$ is broken into $64$ equal droplets. The surface tension of water is $0 . 075N{m}^{- 1}$. In this process the gain in surface energy will be
questions.solution:
By conserving the total volume $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} = 64 \times \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3}\right)$⇒ R = 4r$

Change in surface energy is

$\DeltaU = T \times \DeltaA$, $= T\left[64 \times 4\pi{r}^{2} - 4\pi{R}^{2}\right]$

$= 4\piT{R}^{2}\left[64 \times \dfrac{1}{16} - 1\right] = 12 \times 3 . 14 \times 0 . 075 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$\approx 2 . 8 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

questions.q:
The area of cross-section of a large tank is $0 . 5{m}^{2}$. It has a narrow opening near the bottom having area of cross-section $1{cm}^{2}$. A load of $25kg$ is applied on the water at the top in the tank. Neglecting the speed of water in the tank, the velocity of the water, coming out of the opening at the time when the height of water level in the tank is $40cm$ above the bottom, will be _____ $cm{s}^{- 1}$.

[Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$ ]
questions.solution:
Pressure at point $1$ is ${P}_{1} = {P}_{0}$, Pressure at point $2$ is ${P}_{2} = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{mg}{A}$

Applying Bernoulli's equation at top and bottom

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{1}}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{2}}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2} ⇒ {P}_{0} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}^{2} + 0 = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{mg}{A} + 0 + ρgh$

$⇒ \dfrac{250}{5} + {10}^{3} \times 10 \times 0 . 4 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times {10}^{3} \times {v}^{2}$

$v = 3m{s}^{- 1} = 300cm{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: If $p$ is the density and $η$ is coefficient of viscosity of fluid which flows with a speed $v$ in the pipe of diameter $d$, the correct formula for Reynolds number ${R}_{e}$ is
questions.solution:
Reynolds number is given by, ${R}_{e} = \dfrac{ρvd}{η}$, where, $v =$flow velocity, $d =$hydraulic diameter of the pipe, $ρ =$density of the fluid & $η =$coefficient of viscosity of the fluid.

Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces within a fluid which is subjected to relative internal movement due to different fluid velocities.

questions.q: An ideal fluid of density $800kg{m}^{- 3}$, flows smoothly through a bent pipe (as shown in figure) that tapers in cross-sectional area from a to $\dfrac{a}{2}$. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of pipe is $4100Pa$. At wider section, the velocity of fluid is $\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{6}{ms}^{- 1}$ for $x =$_____ . (Given $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
From equation of continuity,

$a{v}_{1} = \dfrac{a}{2}{v}_{2} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$

From Bernoulli's theorem,

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{1}}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{{v}_{2}}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2} ⇒ {P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = ρ\left[g\left({h}_{2} - {h}_{1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left({{v}_{2}}^{2} - {{v}_{1}}^{2}\right)\right] ⇒ 4100 = 800\left[10\left(- 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}3{{v}_{1}}^{2}\right] ⇒ \dfrac{4100}{800} + 10 = \dfrac{3}{2}{{v}_{1}}^{2} ⇒ {v}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{121}{4 \times 3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{363}}{6}m{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, $x = 363$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity of upper layer of water in a river is $36km{h}^{- 1}$. Shearing stress between horizontal layers of water is ${10}^{- 3}N{m}^{- 2}$. Depth of the river is _____ $m$. (Co-efficient of viscosity of water is ${10}^{- 2}Pas$)
questions.solution:
The viscous force formula is given by,

$F = - ηA\dfrac{d v}{d y}$

Therefore, shear stress $\dfrac{F}{A} = - η\dfrac{d v}{d y}$. Here negative sign tells us that the direction of force is opposite to the velocity gradient.

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{F}{A}\right| = η\dfrac{d v}{d y}$

Now $v = 36 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 10m{s}^{- 1}$ and if the depth is $d$

$\dfrac{d v}{d y} = \dfrac{10}{d}$

$⇒ {10}^{- 3} = {10}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{10}{d} ⇒ d = 100m$

questions.q: A glass tumbler having inner depth of $17 . 5cm$ is kept on a table. A student starts pouring water $\left(\mu = \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$ into it while looking at the surface of water from the above. When he feels that the tumbler is half filled, he stops pouring water. Height of water observed by observer
$= \dfrac{H}{{\mu}_{w}} = \dfrac{H}{( 4 / 3 )} = \dfrac{3H}{4}$

Height of air observed by observer $= 17 . 5 - H$

According to question, both height observed by observer is same.
$\dfrac{3H}{4} = 17 . 5 - H$

$⇒ H = 10cm$

questions.solution:

questions.q: A large number of water drops, each of radius $r$, combine to have a drop of radius $R$. If the surface tension is $T$ and mechanical equivalent of heat is $J$, the rise in heat energy per unit volume will be:
questions.solution:
$n \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$

$∴ {n}^{1 / 3}r = R$

$∴$ Total change in surface energy

$= \left(n\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right) - 4\pi{R}^{2}\right)T$

$⇒ 4\piT\left(n{r}^{2} - {R}^{2}\right)$

$∴$ Heat energy

$= \dfrac{4\piT\left(n{r}^{2} - {R}^{2}\right)}{J \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}} = \dfrac{3T}{J}\left(\dfrac{n{r}^{2}}{{R}^{3}} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

Put $n{r}^{3} = {R}^{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{3T}{J}\left(\dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

questions.q: In an experiment to verify Stokes law, a small spherical ball of radius $r$ and density $ρ$ falls under gravity through a distance $h$ in air before entering a tank of water. If the terminal velocity of the ball inside water is same as its velocity just before entering the water surface, then the value of $h$ is proportional to: (ignore viscosity of air)
questions.solution:
The velocity of ball just before striking the surface of water is given by using kinematical equation of motion under the gravity

${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} - 2gy$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = - 2g ( - h )$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{2gh} . . . ( 1 )$

Now, the terminal velocity of spherical ball inside the water tank is given by,

${v}_{T} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{r}^{2} ( ρ - \sigma ) g}{η} . . . ( 2 )$

After falling through $h$ the velocity of ball should be equal to its terminal velocity.

From equation (1) and (2) we get,

$⇒ \sqrt{2gh} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{r}^{2} ( ρ - \sigma ) g}{η}$

Squaring the above equation, we get

$⇒ h = \dfrac{2}{81}\dfrac{{r}^{4}g ( ρ - \sigma{)}^{2}}{{η}^{2}}$

$⇒ h ∝ {r}^{4}$

questions.q: Water flows m a horizontal tube (see figure). The pressure of water changes by $700N{m}^{- 2}$ between $A$ and $B$ where the area of cross section are $40c{m}^{2}$ and $20c{m}^{2},$ respectively. Find the rate of flow of water through the tube. (density of water $= 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$ )
questions.solution:
Using equation of continuity
$40{V}_{A} = 20{V}_{B}$
$⇒ 2{V}_{A} = {V}_{B}$
Using Bernoulli’s equation
${P}_{A} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{A}^{2} = {P}_{B} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{B}^{2}$
$⇒ {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({V}_{B}^{2} - {V}_{A}^{2}\right)$
$⇒ \DeltaP = \dfrac{1}{2}1000\left({V}_{B}^{2} - \dfrac{{V}_{B}^{2}}{4}\right)$
$⇒ \DeltaP = 500 \times \dfrac{3{V}_{B}^{2}}{4}$
$⇒ {V}_{B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(\DeltaP\right) \times 4}{1500}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(700\right) \times 4}{1500}}\dfrac{m}{s}$
Volume flow rate $= 20 \times 100 \times {V}_{B} = 2732c{m}^{3} / s$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A leak proof cylinder of length $1m,$ made of a metal which has very low coefficient of expansion is floating vertically in water at ${0}^{o}C$ such that its height above the water surface is $20cm .$ When the temperature of water is increased to ${4}^{o}C,$ the height of the cylinder above the water surface becomes $21cm .$ The density of water at $T = {4}^{o}C,$ relative to the density at $T = {0}^{o}C$ is close to:
questions.solution:
According to Archemedes Principle, weight of the body is balanced by the upward thrust force due to buoyancy.

At $0 ° C$, $mg = A ( 100 - 20 ) {ρ}_{0 ° C}g$, where $A$ is area of cross-section of cylinder and ${ρ}_{0 ° C}$ is density of water at $0 ° C$.
At $4 ° C$, $mg = A ( 100 - 21 ) {ρ}_{4 ° C}g$, where ${ρ}_{4 ° C}$ is density of water at $4 ° C$.
$\dfrac{{ρ}_{4 ° C}}{{ρ}_{0 ° C}} = \dfrac{80}{79} = 1.01$

questions.q: Consider a solid sphere of radius $R$ and mass density $ρ\left(r\right) = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}\right), 0 < r \le R .$ The minimum density of a liquid in which it will float is:
questions.solution:
The density of any point inside the sphere is

$ρ = {ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}\right)0 < r \le R$

weight = buoyant force
mg = B

$mg = {ρ}_{L}Vg$
$∫ ρ\left(4\pi{r}^{2}dr\right)g = {ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}g$
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}{ρ}_{0}\left(1 - \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{R}^{2}}\right)4\pi{r}^{2}dr = {ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{R}{ρ}_{0}4\pi\left({r}^{2} - \dfrac{{r}^{4}}{{R}^{2}}\right)dr = {ρ}_{0}4\pi{\left(\dfrac{{r}^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{{r}^{5}}{5{R}^{2}}\right)}_{0}^{R} = {ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$
$\dfrac{2}{5}{ρ}_{0} = {ρ}_{L}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere, of radius R acquires a terminal velocity ${v}_{1}$ when falling (due to gravity) through a viscous fluid having a coefficient of viscosity $η .$ The sphere is broken into 27 identical solid spheres. If each of these spheres acquires a terminal velocity, ${v}_{2},$ when falling through the same fluid, the ratio $\left(\dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}}\right)$ equals:
questions.solution:
If $R$ is the radius of initial drop and $r$ is the radius of new drop, then
$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} = 27 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} ⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{3}$
Terminal velocity,

${v}_{T} ∝ {r}^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \dfrac{{R}^{2}}{{\left(\dfrac{R}{3}\right)}^{2}} = 9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A cubical block of side $0.5m$ floats on water with $30%$ of its volume under water. What is the maximum weight that can be put on the block without fully submerging it under water?

[Take, density of water $= {10}^{3}kg / {m}^{3}$ ]
questions.solution:
In first case, when $30%$ of the cube inside water,
${ρ}_{w}{V}_{in}g = {ρ}_{c}Vg$
$\dfrac{{V}_{in}}{V} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{c}}{{ρ}_{w}} = 0.3$
Additional weight we can put $w$ is,
$V{ρ}_{w}g = {ρ}_{c}Vg + w$
$w = V\left({ρ}_{w} - {ρ}_{c}\right)g$
$= {\left(0.5\right)}^{3} \times 0.7 \times {10}^{3} \times g$
$= 87.5gN$
Addition of mass that we can put $= 87.5kg$

questions.q:
Water from a tap emerges vertically downwards with an initial speed of $1.0m{s}^{- 1}$ . The cross $-$ sectional area of the tap is ${10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}$ . Assume that the pressure is constant throughout the stream of water and that the flow is streamlined. The cross $-$ sectional area of the stream, $0.15m$ below the tap would be:
(Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$ )
questions.solution:
Velocity of water after falling through distance $0.15m$ is
${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$
$= 1 + 2 \times 10 \times 0.15$
${v}^{2} = 4$
$v = 2m / s$
From equation of continuity
${A}_{1}{v}_{1} = {A}_{2}{v}_{2}$
${A}_{2} = \dfrac{{10}^{- 4} \times 1}{2} = 5 \times {10}^{- 5}{m}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A submarine experiences a pressure of $5.05 \times {10}^{6}Pa$ at a depth of ${d}_{1}$ in a sea. When it goes further to a depth of ${d}_{2}$ , it experiences a pressure of $8.08 \times {10}^{6}Pa$ . Then ${d}_{2} - {d}_{1}$ is approximately (density of water $= {10}^{3}kg / {m}^{3}$ and acceleration due to gravity $= 10m{s}^{- 2}$ ):
questions.solution:
The pressure at a depth $d$ is $p = {p}_{0} + ρgd$, here ${p}_{0}$ is the atmospheric pressure.
$∴ {p}_{1} = {p}_{0} + ρg{d}_{1}$
and ${p}_{2} = {p}_{0} + ρg{d}_{2}$
The difference in pressure is ${p}_{2} - {p}_{1} = ρg\left({d}_{2} - {d}_{1}\right)$

Putting the values in the above equation
$8.08 \times {10}^{6} - 5.05 \times {10}^{6} = {10}^{3} \times 10\left({d}_{2} - {d}_{1}\right)$
${d}_{2} - {d}_{1} = \dfrac{3.03 \times {10}^{6}}{{10}^{4}}$
$= 303m$

questions.q: The ratio of surface tensions of mercury and water is given to be $7.5$, while the ratio of their densities is $13.6$. Their contact angles, with glass, are close to $135 °$ and $0 °$, respectively. If it is observed that mercury gets depressed by an amount $h$ in a capillary tube of radius ${r}_{1}$, while water rises by the same amount $h$ in a capillary tube of radius ${r}_{2}$, then the ratio $\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}}$ is close to
questions.solution:
$| {h}_{Hg} | = | {h}_{water} |$

$\dfrac{2{S}_{1}cos{\theta}_{1}}{{ρ}_{1}{r}_{1}g} = \dfrac{2{S}_{2}cos{\theta}_{2}}{{ρ}_{2}{r}_{2}g}$

Therefore, the ratio of the radii of the respective tubes is,

$\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1}} \times \dfrac{{S}_{1}cos{\theta}_{1}}{{S}_{2}cos{\theta}_{2}}$

$\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{13.6} \times 7.5 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} \approx \dfrac{2}{5}$

questions.q: A wooden block floating in a bucket of water has $\dfrac{4}{5}$ of its volume submerged. When certain amount of an oil is poured into the bucket, it is found that the block is just under the oil surface with half of its volume under water and half in oil. The density of oil relative to that of water is:
questions.solution:
Case-1, $\sigmaVg = {ρ}_{w}\dfrac{4}{5}Vg$ …….(I)
Case-2, $\sigmaVg = {ρ}_{w}\dfrac{V}{2}g + {ρ}_{o}\dfrac{V}{2}g$ …….(II)
From eq (I) & (II),
$\dfrac{4}{5}{ρ}_{w} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{w}}{2} + \dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{2}$
$\left(\dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right){ρ}_{w} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{2}$
$\left(\dfrac{8 - 5}{10}\right){ρ}_{w} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{2}$
$\dfrac{{ρ}_{o}}{{ρ}_{w}} = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$

Volume flow rate $= \pi{r}^{2}v = 100\dfrac{l}{min}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{1}{600\pi{r}^{2}}m / sec$

$= \dfrac{1000}{1 \times {10}^{- 3}} \times \dfrac{1}{600\pi{r}^{2}} \times 2r$
$= \dfrac{2000}{0.6\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)} = 21220.66 = 2.1 \times {10}^{4}$

questions.q: A soap bubble, blown by a mechanical pump at the mouth of a tube increases in volume with time at a constant rate. The graph that correctly depicts the time dependence of pressure inside the bubble is given by:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = k$

$⇒ V = kt$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = kt$

$⇒ r = {\left(\dfrac{3k}{4\pi}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}{t}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$

$P - {P}_{0} = \dfrac{4T}{r}$

$⇒ P - {P}_{0} = 4T . \left(\dfrac{3k}{4\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} . \dfrac{1}{t\dfrac{1}{3}}$⇒ P = 4T . \left(\dfrac{3k}{4\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} . \dfrac{1}{t\dfrac{1}{3}} + {P}_{0}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A liquid of density $\rho$ is coming out of a hose pipe of radius a with horizontal speed $v$ and hits a mesh. $50 \%$ of the liquid passes through the mesh unaffected. $25 \%$ looses all of its momentum and $25 \%$ comes back with the same speed. The resultant pressure on the mesh will be:
questions.solution:
Mass per unit time of the liquid = \rhoav Momentum per second carried by liquid $=\rho a v \times v$

Net force due to bounced back liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{1}=2 \times\left[\frac{1}{4} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}\right]$

Net force due to stopped liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}$ pav $^{2}$ Total force,

$\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{F}_{1}+\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}+\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}=\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}$

Net pressure $=\frac{3}{4} \rho v^{2}$

questions.q: The top of a water tank is open to air and its water level is maintained. It is giving out $0.74{m}^{3}$ water per minute through a circular opening of $2cm$ radius in its wall. The depth of the centre of the opening from the level of water in the tank is close to:
questions.solution:
Volume of water flowing out$= Av$, where $A$ is area of opening and $v$ is speed of water from the opening.

$\text{Volume} = \pi{r}^{2}v$

$0 . 74\left(\dfrac{{m}^{3}}{min}\right) = \left(3.14 \times {\left(2 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2} \times \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times H}\right)\dfrac{{m}^{3}}{s} \times \dfrac{60s}{min}$

$⇒ H = {\left(\dfrac{0.74}{60 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times {10}^{- 4}}\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{1}{20}$

$⇒ H = 4.8m$

Hence, the height of water in the tank was $4 . 8m$ from the bottom of the tank.

questions.solution:
Reynolds number

$R = \dfrac{ρvD}{η}$

$D =$ Diameter of litre

Also rate of flow $= \dfrac{volume}{time} = Av$

$\dfrac{V}{t} = \dfrac{\pi{D}^{2}}{4} \times v ⇒ v = \dfrac{4V}{\pi{D}^{2}t}$

$∴ R = \dfrac{ρD}{η} \times \dfrac{4V}{\pi{D}^{2}t}$

$= \dfrac{4ρV}{\piηDt}$

$= \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{3} \times 15 \times {10}^{- 3}}{\pi \times {10}^{- 3} \times 2 \times 5 \times 60}\sqrt{\pi} \times {10}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{10000}{\sqrt{\pi}} \approx 5500$

questions.solution:
$n \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$

$∴ n = \dfrac{{R}^{3}}{{r}^{3}} . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$KE = {U}_{i} - {U}_{f}$

$= n \times 4\pi{r}^{2}T - 4\pi{R}^{2}T$

$= 4\piT ( n{r}^{2} - {R}^{2} )$

$= 4\piT{R}^{2}\left(\dfrac{R}{r} - 1\right)$ from $\left(i\right)$

$\dfrac{Rρ{υ}^{2}}{6} = T\left(\dfrac{R}{r} - 1\right)$

$\dfrac{ρ}{6}{υ}^{2} = T\left(\dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

$υ = \sqrt{\dfrac{6T}{ρ}\left(\dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)}$
